content.about: Expert rows for `rigtune compare --expert`. Each row is a stock row with one setting an engine's own documentation recommends, quoted from the page at the tags in read_at. Written before any comparison was measured with them; not to be adjusted after seeing results. A row that changes numerics (changes_numerics) should be read with --check-answers. `considered` lists every recommendation on those pages that was read and not turned into a row, with the reason.

skip_on_gpu.why: vLLM's own source: "Setting large `max_num_batched_tokens` for A100 reduces throughput, see PR #17885 for more details." (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py EngineArgs.get_batch_defaults, NOTE(Kuntai), v0.29.0 and v0.33.0)

cites.page: docs/configuration/optimization.md, Performance Tuning with Chunked Prefill
cites.quote: For optimal throughput, we recommend setting `max_num_batched_tokens > 8192` especially for smaller models on large GPUs.

settings.value_from: the same section's own example, LLM(model="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct", max_num_batched_tokens=16384); the section also says higher values give better time to first token
settings.default_from: vllm/engine/arg_utils.py EngineArgs.get_batch_defaults (UsageContext.OPENAI_API_SERVER) at both tags: 2048 below 70 GiB and on an A100, 8192 from 70 GiB, 16384 from 160 GiB, where the recommendation is already met and the row would repeat the stock one

cites.quote: This document shows how to use [Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.01318) with vLLM to reduce inter-token latency under medium-to-low QPS (queries per second), memory-bound workloads.
| N-gram | Low to medium gain | Medium gain | Lightweight and easy to enable. |

settings.value_from: docs/features/speculative_decoding/n_gram.md (identical at both tags), whose example is speculative_config={"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "prompt_lookup_max": 4}; passed as written, not through rigtune's own n-gram setting, which also sets prompt_lookup_min 2 where the example leaves it to mirror prompt_lookup_max

cites.quote: Quantizing the KV (Key-Value) cache to FP8 format can significantly reduce its memory footprint. This optimization enables you to store more tokens in memory, leading to improved throughput and support for longer context windows.

settings.value_from: the same page's option 1, "No calibration (default scales)", configured with kv_cache_dtype="fp8"; the page marks calibration with llm-compressor as "[Recommended]", which needs a checkpoint that carries the scales, so this row uses the default scales of 1.0

on_cards_without_it.why: on a card where rigtune does not run vLLM's fp8 (e4m3) cache, Ampere among them, the row uses the page's other fp8 format, which rigtune runs there through FlashInfer (rigtune/backends/vllm.py AMPERE_FP8_KV)

cites.quote: **No extra model available**: Use **NGRAM** (`--speculative-algorithm NGRAM`, CUDA-only).

settings.value_from: the flag alone, every n-gram setting at SGLang's default

cites.quote: For `--speculative-num-steps`, `--speculative-eagle-topk`, and `--speculative-num-draft-tokens`: leave all three unset to use auto-tuning, or set all three explicitly when tuning.

settings.value_from: the head rigtune lists for the model (rigtune/speculative.py EAGLE3_HEADS); the three step settings are left unset, as the quote says. SGLang keeps the head's weights outside --mem-fraction-static, so at the stock row's fraction it may not start, which the comparison then records

cites.quote: Quantized KV cache is a memory optimization technique that primarily benefits throughput by allowing more tokens to be cached, but may introduce minimal accuracy degradation depending on the quantization format used.
**Choose the right format**: Use `fp8_e4m3` for better accuracy (recommended), `fp8_e5m2` for larger dynamic range, or `nvfp4` / `fp4_mx_block16` for maximum memory savings (experimental)

settings.value_from: the format the page marks recommended; the page also warns that without scaling factors in the checkpoint the scales default to 1.0, "which may cause accuracy issues"

cites.quote: **Choose the right format**: Use `fp8_e4m3` for better accuracy (recommended), `fp8_e5m2` for larger dynamic range, or `nvfp4` / `fp4_mx_block16` for maximum memory savings (experimental)

fallback.why: rigtune has not run SGLang's fp8_e4m3 cache on Ampere (it runs fp8_e5m2 there, rigtune/backends/sglang.py kv_dtypes): when fp8_e4m3 fails to start, the row is measured with the page's other fp8 format and the notes say so

cites.quote: `torch.compile` accelerates small models on small batch sizes. You can enable it with `--enable-torch-compile`.

settings.value_from: the flag alone; the page gives no size below which a model counts as small, so the row is offered for every model; a comparison that measures more users than acts_up_to_users says so in its notes

cites.quote: Set the maximum batch size when using torch compile.

acts_up_to_users.why: SGLang compiles batches of up to --torch-compile-max-bs, 32 by default, and runs larger ones as it would without the flag, so the busier levels measure the row outside the small batches the page recommends it for

considered.advice: increase gpu_memory_utilization, or decrease max_num_seqs or max_num_batched_tokens
considered.why_not: only when preemption warnings are frequent: a condition read from a running server, not a setting fixed before it starts

considered.page: docs/configuration/optimization.md, Performance Tuning with Chunked Prefill
considered.why_not: the other direction of the same knob, for inter-token latency; 2048 is already vLLM's default below 70 GiB, so the stock row has it there

considered.page: docs/configuration/conserving_memory.md, Context length and batch size
considered.why_not: advice for a model that runs out of memory; it trades capacity for fitting, not for speed

considered.advice: VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1 with the fastokens package installed
considered.why_not: an environment variable and an extra package, which a rigtune Config cannot set; the page says the change is unlikely to be visible when GPU prefill or decode is the bottleneck
-O2 is the default and -O3 is currently equal to it

considered.advice: EAGLE, MTP, draft models and PARD: high gain at low QPS
considered.why_not: each needs a second model or a checkpoint's own head, chosen per model; rigtune's own search (--speculative all) offers the ones it can verify

considered.advice: Suffix decoding: "Low to medium gain", "No extra draft model; dynamic speculation depth"
considered.why_not: the same gain the guide gives n-gram, which is the row; suffix decoding also needs a package a stock vLLM install lacks ("Suffix Decoding requires [Arctic Inference]"), so as a row it would be skipped wherever the stock engine runs. rigtune's own search (--speculative all) offers it where the package is installed

considered.page: docs/docs/advanced_features/hyperparameter_tuning.mdx, Tune --mem-fraction-static to increase KV cache pool capacity
considered.advice: set --mem-fraction-static as high as possible while reserving 5-8 GB; check available_gpu_mem in the log just before the server is ready
considered.why_not: the 5-8 GB is checked on a launched server (available_gpu_mem, measured after CUDA graphs are captured), so the guide gives no value to set before launch; a fraction computed from it would need a size for the CUDA graphs that the guide does not give

considered.advice: --schedule-conservativeness 0.3 when token usage stays under 0.9 with requests queued, 1.3 on frequent retractions
considered.why_not: conditional on the running server's log
"for some models, especially at large tensor parallelism sizes"; no value is given for one GPU
fp8 weights are part of rigtune's own search and change the model rather than the server; lpm is for workloads with many shared prefixes, a property of the traffic the guide leaves to the operator
the page recommends fp8_e4m3, which is the row

considered.page: docs/docs/advanced_features/server_arguments.mdx, the tips before the argument table
